trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use morning for any pre-departure preparations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to the city center. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a leisurely walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' featuring Gaudí's Casa Batlló exterior (free from outside), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Window-shop and soak in the Modernista architecture of the Eixample grid streets.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Eixample nightlife scene. Head to the Esquerra de l'Eixample neighborhood (known as 'Gayxample') for affordable pre-drinks at one of the many bars. Try Bar Calders or a local cervecería for €2–3 draft beers. End the night with a stroll down La Rambla to get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a €2–3 croissant and coffee at the airport café upon landing.
meals.lunch: Pick up a bocadillo (sandwich) from a local bakery or supermarket (Mercadona/Lidl) near the hotel for under €4.
meals.dinner: Try a budget menú del día (set menu) at a local restaurant in Eixample — typically €10–13 for starter, main, dessert, bread, and a drink. Look for places on side streets away from main tourist areas.

day_by_day.notes: Get a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) at the airport or any metro station — it covers all metro, bus, and tram journeys and will save money throughout the trip. August is very hot in Barcelona (30°C+), so carry water and wear sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early (before the heat peaks) with a visit to the iconic Sagrada Família. Book tickets online in advance to avoid queues — entry with tower access costs around €26–32, but the basic entry (~€20) is budget-friendly. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, one of the most extraordinary architectural works in the world. The surrounding streets and park provide great exterior views for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell. The monumental zone requires a ticket (~€10, book online), but the surrounding park and terraces are free and offer stunning city views. Spend the hottest part of the afternoon exploring the colorful mosaic terraces and Gaudí-designed pathways. Afterward, head back to the hotel for a siesta during peak heat (2 PM–5 PM) — a very local habit.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) after 6 PM when it cools slightly. Wander through narrow medieval streets, visit the free exterior of the Barcelona Cathedral, and explore Plaça Reial. As night falls, enjoy the lively bar scene around Plaça Reial and El Born neighborhood — many bars have happy hour deals from 6–9 PM.

meals.breakfast: Grab a traditional breakfast at a local café near the hotel — café amb llet (coffee with milk) and a tostada con tomate (toast with tomato) for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Sagrada Família or a falafel/kebab wrap in the Gothic Quarter for €5–8.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — a classic, affordable tapas bar. Order pan con tomate, croquetas, and house cava. Budget €12–15 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least a few days ahead — they sell out fast in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes; you'll cover 8–10 km today.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana, a stunning UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Guided tours cost around €20, but attending a morning concert (sometimes as low as €15–18) is a more immersive and cost-effective option. Alternatively, admire the ornate exterior for free. Then stroll through El Born neighborhood, one of Barcelona's hippest areas with street art and independent shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Barceloneta Beach for a few hours. The beach is free — bring your own snacks and water from a supermarket. Rent a paddleboard or kayak if budget allows (~€10–15/hour). Walk along the Passeig Marítim seafront promenade and admire the Barcelona coastline. Stop by the striking W Barcelona Hotel and the Port Olímpic area to see modern architectural contrasts.
day_by_day.evening: Port Olímpic transforms into a nightlife hub after dark. Explore the marina bars and clubs — many have free entry before midnight. For a more local and cheaper vibe, head to the bars along Carrer del Parlament in Sant Antoni neighborhood, a trendy but affordable area popular with young locals.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh fruit, yogurt, and pastries from Mercat de Santa Caterina (a beautiful Modernista market near El Born) — budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh bocadillo or empanada from a beach kiosk, or buy supplies from a supermarket for a beach picnic — €5–7.
meals.dinner: Try La Cova Fumada in Barceloneta (cash only, arrives early as it closes when food runs out) — famous for the original bombas and affordable seafood tapas, ~€10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta Beach gets extremely crowded in August. Go early afternoon or late afternoon for a better experience. Keep an eye on your belongings — pickpocketing is common in tourist beach areas.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Fundació Joan Miró on Montjuïc hill — a beautifully designed building by Josep Lluís Sert housing vibrant works of the surrealist artist. Entry is around €14 (check for discounts). Take the metro to Paral·lel and then the Funicular de Montjuïc (covered by your T-Casual card) up the hill. Explore the surrounding gardens and get panoramic views of the city for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Montjuïc. Visit the free exterior of the Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys (1992 Olympics venue) and the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe — a landmark of modernist architecture open for ~€10. Walk through the beautiful Jardins de Laribal (free) and enjoy the fountains. Take the cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc, ~€12 return) for aerial views, or walk back down via scenic paths.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for the evening. Visit the Magic Fountain of Montjuïc (Font Màgica) — a spectacular free light and music show held on Thursday–Sunday evenings in summer, starting around 9:30 PM. This is one of Barcelona's best free attractions. Afterward, explore the nightlife on Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner in Eixample.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and croissant at a neighborhood café in Eixample — €3–4.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a supermarket or a menú del día near Montjuïc for €10–12.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda or similar neighborhood bodega in Eixample — affordable wine, cheese, and charcuterie plates. Budget €10–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Font Màgica show schedule in advance — it runs Thursday to Sunday in summer. Montjuïc involves a lot of walking on hills; wear comfortable shoes and bring water. The Funicular is included in your T-Casual metro card.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the final morning at the Mercat de la Boqueria on La Rambla — one of Europe's most famous food markets. While some stalls are pricey and touristy, you can find affordable fresh fruit, olives, and local snacks. Browse the colorful displays and soak up the atmosphere. Then walk through the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) plaza — a popular skateboarding spot with striking modern architecture by Richard Meier. MACBA entry is ~€12 but the exterior and plaza are free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Do a final walk through the Gothic Quarter and El Born to pick up any last souvenirs (avoid tourist shops on La Rambla — try local shops on side streets for better prices). Visit the free Plaça de Sant Jaume and the Roman ruins visible through the windows of the Temple d'August (free or small fee). Pack your bags and prepare for departure, depending on your flight time.
day_by_day.evening: If your flight is late, enjoy a farewell dinner in Eixample near the hotel. Otherwise, head to the airport via Aerobus or Metro L9 (allow 40–60 minutes from the city center). Do a final stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to say goodbye to the Modernista skyline.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit and a smoothie from La Boqueria market stalls — €4–6.
meals.lunch: Menú del día at a local restaurant in the Gothic Quarter or El Born — €10–13.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a classic Catalan restaurant in Eixample — try escalivada, pa amb tomàquet, and patatas bravas. Budget €12–16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate for 5 days (excluding flights and accommodation): Transport ~€25, Attractions ~€60–80, Food ~€60–75, Nightlife/drinks ~€30–40. Total approximate spend: €175–220. Always carry some cash as many small bars and markets are cash-only. Learn a few words of Catalan (gràcies, bon dia) — locals appreciate the effort!

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample district. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely self-guided walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera — iconic Modernista facades right on your doorstep in Eixample. Browse the upscale boutiques and soak in the architectural grandeur without needing a ticket.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) for a relaxed first evening. Stroll the narrow medieval lanes, visit Plaça Reial, and settle into a welcoming tapas bar for dinner. End the night with a drink at one of the atmospheric bars around Plaça George Orwell.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a café con leche and a croissant at the airport or hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick menú del día (set lunch menu) near the hotel in Eixample — typically €12–16 for three courses including wine. Try Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca.
meals.dinner: Tapas dinner in the Gothic Quarter. Bar del Pla (Carrer de la Montcada area) offers excellent patatas bravas, croquetas, and pan con tomate for around €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pick up a T-Casual metro card (10 trips, ~€11.35) at the airport or any metro station to save money on transport all week.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Book the first morning slot (9:00 or 9:30 AM) to beat the crowds. The guided tour reveals Gaudí's intricate symbolism, the towering naves, and the stunning stained-glass light show. Allow 2–2.5 hours. The basilica is a short metro or walk from Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take the metro to Park Güell. Explore Gaudí's whimsical mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona. The Monumental Zone requires a timed ticket (book in advance, ~€10). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert — Attend a live performance at this UNESCO-listed Art Nouveau masterpiece. Check the schedule in advance and book tickets (€25–50 depending on the concert). The ornate stained-glass ceiling and sculpted interior are as much a spectacle as the music itself.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby Eixample café. Try a traditional Catalan breakfast of pa amb tomàquet (bread rubbed with tomato) and fresh orange juice at Forn de Sant Jaume or similar bakery (€5–8).
meals.lunch: Casual lunch near Park Güell or back in Gràcia neighbourhood. La Pepita (Carrer de Montserrat) serves creative bocadillos and salads for €10–15.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner near the Palau de la Música in El Born district. Try Bar Brutal or El Xampanyet for wine, cheese, and tapas (€20–30 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Palau de la Música tickets well in advance — both sell out weeks ahead, especially in August. Sagrada Família with guided tour costs approximately €26–33 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Barceloneta Beach & Chiringuito Hopping — Head to Barceloneta Beach for a morning swim and sunbathe session before the afternoon heat peaks. The beach is easily reached by metro (Barceloneta stop). Stroll the passeig and explore the beachfront chiringuitos (beach bars) for a refreshing agua de coco or fresh fruit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Paella & Tapas Dinner at Passeig Marítim — Enjoy an extended, leisurely Catalan lunch (Spaniards eat lunch late, 2:00–4:00 PM) at one of the seafront restaurants along the Passeig Marítim. Order a traditional paella de mariscos or fideuà to share. After lunch, walk along the boardwalk toward Port Olímpic and relax. Visit the nearby Barceloneta neighbourhood's market or browse local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront Nightlife at Port Olímpic — Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife at the Port Olímpic marina. The cluster of open-air bars and clubs comes alive after 11:00 PM. Start with a cocktail at one of the terrace bars overlooking the marina, then move to a club if the mood strikes. CDLC and Pacha Barcelona are popular mid-range options.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or pick up fresh pastries and coffee at a Barceloneta café before hitting the beach (€5–7).
meals.lunch: Seafront paella lunch at Passeig Marítim — La Mar Salada or Salamanca restaurant offer quality paella at €15–22 per person for the dish, plus drinks. This doubles as the 'afternoon activity.'
meals.dinner: Light pre-nightlife dinner or skip a formal dinner — graze on pintxos or a bocadillo at a Port Olímpic bar before the nightlife begins (€10–15). Stay hydrated with agua con gas.

day_by_day.notes: August beach days are hot (30°C+). Bring sunscreen SPF 50+, a hat, and water. Nightlife in Barcelona starts very late — clubs don't fill up until midnight or 1:00 AM. Pace yourself if you plan to stay out late.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning after nightlife — sleep in and enjoy a slow hotel breakfast or brunch. By mid-morning, visit the Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau, a stunning UNESCO-listed Art Nouveau hospital complex designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner, just a 10-minute walk from the Sagrada Família. Far less crowded than other landmarks, it's a hidden architectural gem (entry ~€16).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the El Born neighbourhood on foot — visit the Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (free entry), a stunning Gothic church built by the people of the Ribera neighbourhood. Browse the trendy boutiques, vintage shops, and art galleries along Carrer del Rec and surrounding streets. Stop at the El Born Cultural Centre to see the ruins of the 1714 city beneath a striking iron-and-glass structure.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop bar evening in Eixample — Barcelona's rooftop bar scene is world-class. Visit the rooftop of La Barceloneta Hotel or the terrace at Hotel Majestic on Passeig de Gràcia for sunset cocktails with skyline views (cocktails €12–18). Then head to the Eixample Esquerra (Left Eixample, also known as 'Gayxample') for a vibrant bar-hopping evening along Carrer del Consell de Cent.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at Federal Café in Sant Antoni neighbourhood — avocado toast, eggs, and specialty coffee (€12–18). A favourite among locals.
meals.lunch: Pintxos lunch in El Born — Bar Cañete or Euskal Etxea serve excellent Basque-style pintxos for €2–4 per piece. Budget €15–20 for a satisfying spread with a glass of txakoli.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Eixample before the rooftop bar session. Cervecería Catalana (if not visited Day 1) or Parking Pizza on Londres street for a more casual, affordable option (€15–22 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau is often overlooked by tourists — arrive at opening (10:00 AM) for a peaceful experience. Santa Maria del Mar is free but donations are appreciated. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for El Born's cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Montjuïc — Take the cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) or metro/bus up to the hilltop park for panoramic city views. Explore the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry), walk through the gardens, and visit the Fundació Joan Miró if contemporary art interests you (€14). The hilltop is cooler than the city below — perfect for a morning outing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and spend your final afternoon revisiting favourite spots or doing any last-minute shopping. Mercat de Sant Antoni (recently renovated covered market near Eixample) is excellent for local produce, books, and artisan goods. Alternatively, revisit Passeig de Gràcia for souvenir shopping or visit the interior of Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) if not done earlier (~€25–35 each, book ahead).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special restaurant to close out the trip. Disfrutar (if splurging — Michelin-starred, book months ahead) or a more mid-range option like Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample for excellent Catalan cuisine with natural wines (€35–50 per person). End the night with a final walk along the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia and a nightcap at a rooftop or jazz bar.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel. Enjoy a traditional ensaïmada (spiral pastry) with café amb llet as a final Catalan morning treat (€5–8).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Montjuïc — pack a picnic from the hotel or a nearby supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) to enjoy in the gardens, or grab a bite at the Fundació Joan Miró café (€10–15).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Eixample. Bodega Sepúlveda (Carrer de Sepúlveda) offers a warm, neighbourhood atmosphere with seasonal Catalan dishes and a well-curated wine list — budget €35–50 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is early on Day 6, pack the night before and confirm your airport transfer. The Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya to the airport runs frequently (€6.75 one-way) and is the most convenient mid-range option. Allow at least 2.5 hours before a morning flight.

day_by_day.evening: Paella & Tapas Dinner at Passeig Marítim — head to the seafront for an authentic Catalan dining experience. Reserve a table at a premium seafront restaurant such as Restaurante 1881 per Sagardi or Agua, enjoying fresh seafood paella, pan con tomate, and Catalan wine as the Mediterranean sun sets over the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or at airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at a rooftop terrace café on Passeig de Gràcia — jamón ibérico, Manchego, artisan bread, and a glass of Cava
meals.dinner: Premium seafront dining at Passeig Marítim — signature seafood paella, grilled gambas al ajillo, crema catalana, and a curated Catalan wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer before departure. Request early check-in at the hotel if possible given the 13:00 arrival. Keep the first afternoon relaxed to avoid jet lag. Book dinner reservation in advance as prime seafront tables fill quickly in August.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — begin the day with a skip-the-line private guided tour of Gaudí's legendary basilica, just a short walk or taxi from Eixample. A dedicated architect-guide will reveal the symbolic stonework, the Nativity and Passion facades, and the breathtaking forest-like interior. Ascend one of the towers via private lift for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Chiringuito Hopping — after the tour, head to Barceloneta Beach for a premium beach afternoon. Reserve a sunbed and parasol at a top-tier chiringuito such as Ànima Beach or Boca Grande Beach Club. Sip fresh mojitos, enjoy ceviche and grilled octopus, and swim in the warm Mediterranean waters.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront Nightlife at Port Olímpic — as the sun dips, transition seamlessly into Barcelona's legendary nightlife scene at Port Olímpic marina. Begin with sunset cocktails at a terrace bar overlooking the yachts, then move to one of the open-air clubs such as Pacha or Opium Barcelona for a world-class DJ night under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel or a nearby upscale café — freshly squeezed juices, eggs benedict, artisan pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Premium chiringuito dining at Barceloneta — grilled octopus, fresh ceviche, patatas bravas, and signature cocktails at Ànima Beach Club
meals.dinner: Pre-club dinner at a Port Olímpic waterfront restaurant — grilled sea bass, lobster bisque, and a bottle of white Albariño before the nightlife begins

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família private tour well in advance — August is peak season and slots sell out weeks ahead. Sunbed reservations at premium chiringuitos should also be pre-booked. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the morning basilica visit; bring a change of clothes or beach bag for the afternoon transition. Port Olímpic clubs typically pick up after midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Late, leisurely start after the nightlife evening. Enjoy a slow gourmet brunch at the hotel or at Brunch & Cake in Eixample. Afterward, explore the Eixample neighbourhood's hidden architectural gems — visit Casa Milà (La Pedrera) with a private guided tour, including exclusive access to the rooftop terrace and the Espai Gaudí exhibition in the attic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) on a private architecture-focused walking tour. Discover the Roman ruins beneath the city, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the labyrinthine medieval streets. Stop at a luxury artisan shop for handcrafted Catalan souvenirs. Conclude with a visit to the Pont del Bisbe bridge for a perfect architectural photograph.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert — attend a live performance at the UNESCO-listed Art Nouveau concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Arrive early to admire the stained-glass ceiling, ornate mosaics, and sculpted columns before the performance begins. Dress code is smart-elegant.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet brunch at Brunch & Cake Eixample — avocado toast with smoked salmon, acai bowls, freshly baked croissants, and cold-brew coffee
meals.lunch: Tapas lunch in the Gothic Quarter at El Xampanyet — house cava, anchovies, boquerones, and artisan cheeses in a historic bodega setting
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Llamber restaurant near El Born — creative Catalan small plates, seasonal tasting menu, and natural wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: La Pedrera private tours include rooftop access — spectacular at any time but especially beautiful in morning light. Book Palau de la Música concert tickets well in advance; select a classical or flamenco fusion program for the most immersive experience. Smart-casual attire required for the concert. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot with a local guide for hidden details.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Montjuïc — take a private cable car ride up to the hilltop for panoramic views of Barcelona and the Mediterranean. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró, a world-class modern art museum housed in a stunning rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert. Explore the Jardins de Laribal, a series of terraced gardens with fountains and sculptures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and visit the El Born neighbourhood for a curated luxury shopping experience — browse high-end Catalan design boutiques, concept stores, and artisan jewellery makers along Carrer del Rec and surroundings. Stop at the El Born Cultural Centre to admire the 18th-century archaeological ruins beneath its iron-and-glass structure.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive rooftop cocktail experience — head to the rooftop bar of the Mandarin Oriental Barcelona or Hotel Arts for sunset cocktails with sweeping city views. Then transition to a premium nightclub experience — secure VIP table service at Sutton Club or Shôko Barcelona for an elevated, curated nightlife evening with bottle service and Barcelona's social elite.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or specialty café near Eixample — full Catalan breakfast with pa amb tomàquet, local charcuterie, fresh fruit, and café con leche
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas bar, booking essential) or Bar Calders in El Born — creative modern tapas in a relaxed setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Disfrutar (two Michelin stars) or Cinc Sentits — avant-garde Catalan tasting menu with wine pairing; one of Barcelona's finest dining experiences

day_by_day.notes: Disfrutar and Tickets require reservations months in advance — book immediately upon confirming your trip. The Montjuïc cable car operates weather permitting; have a backup plan (taxi to the hilltop) if needed. VIP table reservations at Sutton or Shôko should be arranged via the hotel concierge for seamless entry and premium service.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Barcelona — visit Park Güell with a private early-access guided tour before the crowds arrive. Explore Gaudí's surreal mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and the winding viaducts set against a backdrop of pine-covered hills and city views. A fitting architectural farewell to the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Eixample for a final indulgent afternoon — enjoy a spa session at the hotel or a nearby luxury wellness centre. Then take a final stroll along Passeig de Gràcia for last-minute luxury shopping at Loewe, Massimo Dutti, or local Catalan design houses. Pick up premium local products — craft gin, artisan olive oil, or Catalan wine — as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a landmark Barcelona restaurant — dine at Lasarte (three Michelin stars, Chef Martín Berasategui) for an extraordinary final evening. Savour an elaborate tasting menu celebrating the finest Basque-Catalan cuisine with an exceptional wine list. A truly memorable conclusion to a luxury Barcelona experience.

meals.breakfast: Light, early breakfast at the hotel before the Park Güell visit — fresh fruit, yoghurt, pastries, and coffee to prepare for the morning walk
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a Passeig de Gràcia terrace restaurant — grilled vegetables, Iberian ham croquetas, and a glass of Rioja Reserva
meals.dinner: Gala farewell dinner at Lasarte (three Michelin stars) — full tasting menu with sommelier-curated wine pairing; approximately 3–4 hours of dining excellence

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell early-access tickets (before 8:00 AM) must be booked well in advance and are strictly timed — confirm with a private tour operator. Lasarte reservations should be made months ahead; dress code is smart-elegant. If departing early the next morning, arrange a private airport transfer the night before. Consider storing luggage at the hotel on the final day to enjoy a free afternoon without bags.
